atoms.a: In 2013, a woman named Alicia Garza wrote a message on Facebook. She was very sad and angry because a man who had shot a Black teenager named Trayvon Martin was not sent to prison. Her friend added the words: “Black Lives Matter.” That was the beginning of the Black Lives Matter movement.

In 2014, there were big protests in Ferguson, Missouri. A police officer shot a Black teenager named Michael Brown. Many people thought this was unfair. They said: “Hands up, don’t shoot!” The Black Lives Matter movement became more famous.

In 2020, the world saw a video of George Floyd, a Black man, being killed by a police officer in Minneapolis. George Floyd said, “I can’t breathe,” but the officer didn’t stop. This shocked millions of people. There were protests all over the USA and also in other countries. Many people held signs that said: “Black Lives Matter.”
The movement that rose through those incidents wants to stop racism and police violence against Black people. It also wants justice and equal rights for everyone – no matter their skin colour.

atoms.b: The Black Lives Matter movement wanted to fight against ((racism)) and discrimination.
It began in the United States but became a ((global)) movement. People in many countries had joined the protests to show their support.
The protesters said that Black people did not have the same ((rights)) as white people.
One important goal of the movement was to make sure that ((all_people)) were treated fairly—no matter their skin colour, religion, or background.
Many people also wanted changes in the ((education)) system.
They said that schools, workplaces, and housing should have been more ((inclusive)) and equal for everyone.
The movement was peaceful, but it was also very ((powerful)). People wanted their voices to be heard, and they wanted real change in society.
